name: Zhixiang Fan
intro: I am a PhD student in Design at Tsinghua University’s Academy of Arts & Design, with a background in landscape architecture. I study how people understand, create and interact with three-dimensional environments.
research: I focus on translating spatial design knowledge into forms that are computable and interactive, enabling reconstructed or generated 3D environments to be understood, inspected, and modified.

projects.title: Semantic 3D Gaussian Splatting
projects.subtitle: From reconstructed geometry to objects we can query and interact with.
projects.summary: An interactive web system that combines language-aligned 3D Gaussian representations with object-level spatial information. Users can explore a reconstructed scene, select semantic objects and interact through language.
projects.role: Semantic processing pipeline, object-state extraction and web interaction system.
projects.question: How can a visually reconstructed environment become a scene whose objects and spatial relationships can be queried and used in interaction?
projects.approach: The pipeline combines SAM, CLIP, LangSplat and ResGS for open-vocabulary 3D semantics. DBSCAN groups spatial features into object locations; an explicit world state connects these objects to a Three.js viewer and LLM interaction.
projects.outcome: The prototype connects offline semantic feature processing with real-time browser rendering, semantic picking and language-based spatial interaction. It supports scenes containing millions of Gaussians.
projects.scope: System development integrating existing reconstruction and semantic representation methods.

projects.title: Axis at WAIC
projects.subtitle: Minecraft scene creation, character skins and motion-based play.
projects.summary: A team-built creative platform presented at WAIC, connecting AI-assisted Minecraft scene and skin generation with body-driven gameplay. Minecraft serves as a concrete environment for creating content and trying it through interaction.
projects.role: World model technology and product lead; platform architecture, model integration and web runtime development.
projects.question: How can content generation and physical interaction become part of one accessible creative workflow?
projects.approach: Axis coordinates text, image and 3D generation services with task state and a scene runtime. The WAIC demonstration brings together scene creation, character skin generation and camera-based motion interaction.
projects.outcome: A working product and exhibition demonstration connecting creation with play. The platform is being extended beyond its initial Minecraft environment.
projects.scope: Collaborative product. My work focuses on the creation platform and its technical integration. The motion-recognition algorithms were developed primarily by teammates.
projects.mediaNote: Scenes, character skins and body-driven play

projects.title: 4D Reconstruction of Suturing
projects.subtitle: Reconstructing a changing workspace from four camera views.
projects.summary: A medical reconstruction project using four camera views and self-collected recordings of a doctor performing suturing. We use 4D Gaussian Splatting to reconstruct the changing scene over time.
projects.role: Work on the multi-camera capture and 4D reconstruction pipeline within a collaborative project.
projects.question: How can a compact multi-camera setup capture and reconstruct a fine-grained procedure with moving hands, instruments and frequent occlusion?
projects.approach: Our team records the suturing procedure from four camera views and reconstructs the temporal scene using 4D Gaussian Splatting. The work connects data acquisition with dynamic reconstruction and inspection of the resulting sequence.
projects.outcome: A reconstruction prototype on self-collected suturing recordings. The project extends earlier practical work with dynamic Gaussian reconstruction on public datasets.
projects.scope: Ongoing research on dynamic reconstruction from self-collected, four-camera recordings.

projects.title: Design Skills for Chinese Gardens
projects.subtitle: Making spatial design knowledge inspectable and executable.
projects.summary: I describe spatial design rules in natural language and organize them into reusable Design Skills that guide a lightweight LLM to construct scenes and models. Examples include Chinese gardens, temples and imagined mountain landscapes.
projects.role: Spatial design representation, skill system and scene-generation workflow.
projects.question: How can a designer’s knowledge of movement, viewing and spatial sequence become usable by a generation agent while remaining open to human judgment?
projects.approach: Spatial design rules are expressed in language and organized into reusable Design Skills. A lightweight LLM uses these skills to build the scenes and models shown here. WorldSpec represents objects and spatial relationships independently of the rendering backend; navigation and visibility checks support local repair. Users can edit parameters, lock regions and inspect the design rationale.
projects.outcome: An implemented creation–inspection–repair workflow with Three.js and Minecraft outputs, including accept/reject and undo/redo operations. Current scenes provide a testbed for spatial relationships and interaction.
projects.scope: Research prototype. Cultural design claims require domain validation; the system does not treat aesthetics as a universal numerical score.
projects.mediaNote: Design principles, generated scenes and local revision

tasks: Lead Axis development, building server infrastructure, model-service integrations and a web 3D runtime from scratch to connect scene generation with interactive applications.
Develop prototypes for VR/AR applications and embodied interaction, connecting reconstructed or generated environments with user exploration and scene editing.
Investigate streaming first-person video understanding for personal agents, using M3-Agent and YOLO-assisted processing to study how people, objects and events are captured in memory.
Design a multimodal processing workspace for personal-agent development, preserving raw inputs and generating memory text with traceable source evidence and processing history.
Evaluate AI tutoring interactions, including answer guessing, verbalization of mathematical formulas and behavior across long conversations.
Build resumable extraction and validation workflows for 592 conversations and 9,072 contextual messages from approximately 11 GB of cloud JSONL data.
Turn real learning conversations into traceable model issues and product feedback to inform data cleaning, dialogue strategies and interaction improvements.

practice.role: AI Center Intern · Autonomous Driving Simulation
tasks: Construct Wuhan road networks and 3D environments using OSM, RoadRunner, SketchUp and Blender, and integrate them into UE4/CARLA.
Investigate 3DGS scene reconstruction and prototype a closed perception–decision–control loop for autonomous driving.
Design scenario tests and quantitative evaluation workflows to reproduce complex road conditions and assess end-to-end driving models.
